lede: The biggest thing on the board this week is Wednesday's County Commissioner meeting, where the BOCC will ratify a policy change at Pinion Park that drops income eligibility to 80% AMI — a quiet threshold shift that determines who actually gets a deed-restricted unit in this valley. Alongside that, Tuesday's Town Council work sessions dig into the Comprehensive Plan and a proposed third-party audit of rental housing policies, and the Housing Authority Subcommittee takes up a real exception request from homeowners needing a roof on their deed-restricted unit at Gold Run.

notable.stake: Rental housing audit and Comprehensive Plan goals up for substantive Council review.
Martin exception request decides whether deed-restricted owners can fund a $47K roof repair.
BOCC vote to shift Pinion Park income eligibility to 80% AMI changes who qualifies for a unit.
Land Use Code definition changes being shaped before any public hearing is held.
